purpose: Identify publicly reusable individual dry-matter-intake data for adult beef cattle on pasture relevant to issue #6.

sources.title: Statistical Methodologies for the Prediction of Dry Matter Intake in Beef Cattle Raised on Pasture
sources.reportedPopulation: 881 animals from 38 Brazilian studies; paper describes a study-level holdout of 15 studies and 77 animals.
sources.dataAvailabilityStatement: This manuscript relies on confidential private data that cannot be disclosed.
sources.decision: Exclude from numerical validation. The paper license applies to the manuscript; its explicit data statement does not make the underlying individual records public. Do not reconstruct individual observations from tables or figures.

sources.title: Differences in Dry Matter Intake in Grazing and Drylot Beef Cattle
sources.publicationLicense: No separate open-data license for underlying data found on repository record.
sources.reportedPopulation: 163 beef cattle across four experimental groups and two grazing seasons (2024 and 2025). The abstract says pasture DMI was estimated with an LSTM; drylot intake was measured with automated equipment.
sources.decision: Do not score as independent pasture-DMI validation: no openly licensed individual data file was found on the repository record, and the pasture target described in the abstract is model-estimated rather than a direct field measurement.

sources.title: Herbage mass and allowance and animal genotype affect daily herbage intake, productivity, and efficiency of beef cows grazing native subtropical grassland
sources.publicationLicense: Open full-text article in PMC; no separate license for individual data located.
sources.reportedPopulation: 24 to 36 adult multiparous Hereford, Angus, and crossbred beef cows across eight paddocks and six periods in native subtropical grassland. Herbage intake was estimated using the C32:C33 n-alkane ratio; cow weight/condition and calf ADG/weaning outcomes were also reported.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The accessible article reports methods, group/treatment summaries, and results. No downloadable individual-data package, repository DOI, or data-specific reuse license was located in the article record or full-text page during this review.
sources.decision: Retain as a relevant peer-reviewed methodological and population reference only. Do not reconstruct individual observations from tables/figures or score engine accuracy: no reusable individual file was located, intake is estimated by a tracer method, and calf ADG is not the approved adult-cattle ADG target.

sources.title: Herbage selection, intake and digestibility in grazing beef cattle
sources.publicationLicense: The full-text copy states © 2015 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved; no separate license for underlying data found.
sources.reportedPopulation: Twenty nonlactating Angus cows averaging 50 ± 12 months and 525 ± 55 kg grazed mixed pasture for a 28-day study; individual forage intake was estimated with n-alkanes.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The accessible article reports a group mean and standard deviation for grazing forage intake and describes per-cow estimates, but no downloadable per-cow data, data repository record, or data-specific reuse license was located.
sources.decision: Retain as a strong population and measurement-method reference, but exclude from supervised target data: the accessible result is aggregate, the measured grazing outcome is herbage intake rather than documented total DMI including supplement, and no reusable individual records were located. Do not reconstruct rows from the reported mean or figures.

sources.title: Forage intake and digesta kinetics of lactating beef cattle differing in feed efficiency while grazing Idaho rangelands
sources.publicationLicense: No separate data-specific reuse license for cow-level records identified; the article's shared example data/code are not the study observations.
sources.reportedPopulation: Twenty-four 2-year-old lactating Angus × Hereford cows, split into efficient and inefficient groups, grazed Idaho rangeland in spring and summer periods; forage intake was estimated individually using a dosed-alkane method.
sources.dataAvailabilityStatement: The article shares example datasets and corrected SAS code for the nonlinear procedure on OSF; these are not the animal records from the grazing experiment.
sources.publicDataAssessment: No cow-level grazing DMI file, animal-period rows, data repository deposit, or data-specific reuse terms were found. The open OSF material is explicitly described as example datasets and analysis code.
sources.decision: Retain as a recent population and measurement-method reference, but exclude from reusable supervised data: the accessible OSF files are examples/code, not grazing-cohort records, and no row-level animal data or reuse terms were located. Do not treat example inputs or article summaries as field observations.

sources.title: Developing and validating a model to predict the dry matter intake of grazing lactating beef cows
sources.publicationLicense: The article is open access; no separate license or public deposit for the underlying individual DMI records was identified.
sources.reportedPopulation: The calibration study reports 94 DMI measurements on 106 beef or beef-dairy crossbred cows; its model was also applied to a separate herd of 60 lactating beef cows two years later.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The accessible article and institutional full-text copy report model results but no downloadable animal-period microdata, repository DOI, or data-specific reuse license for the cow-level DMI records.
sources.decision: Retain as a highly relevant mature beef-cow pasture methods reference, but exclude from supervised data until individual records, animal/trial keys, and reuse terms are published or authorized. Published model metrics cannot substitute for the source rows.

sources.title: Characterization of individual beef cattle water intake
sources.publicationLicense: Article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; this is not a license for the underlying individual records.
sources.reportedPopulation: 2,084 beef animals from 2019–2024 at two West Virginia sites; 130,000+ daily records of individual water intake, DMI, and body weight across grazing and drylot systems. Grazing records are from crossbred steers.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The article presents cohort and group summaries. No data availability statement, downloadable individual dataset, repository DOI, or data-specific reuse license was found on the accessible full-text page.
sources.decision: Exclude from the issue #109 adult-cow target: the article states that its grazing records are exclusively from crossbred steers, so it does not provide the required mature-cow population even though it reports individual DMI and BW. Do not use article summaries as individual observations; no downloadable individual records or data-specific reuse terms were found. Revisit only if an adult-cow cohort and reusable underlying records are separately provided.

sources.title: Generalizable long short-term memory models for beef cattle DMI under grazing
sources.publicationLicense: Open Access article under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; this license covers the article and does not by itself license the underlying data.
sources.reportedPopulation: Individual daily DMI, body weight, water and climate records for beef cattle across grazing and drylot cohorts, including strictly held-out 2023 grazing animals; grazing cohort includes Bos taurus/crossbred steers in West Virginia.
sources.dataAvailabilityStatement: Data may be available by contacting the corresponding author.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The publisher's full text names no public data repository or downloadable microdata file. The statement indicates possible author-mediated access, not an open download or reusable data license.
sources.decision: Use as a peer-reviewed methods and benchmark reference only while prioritizing open data. Do not reproduce its evaluation from aggregate article metrics or treat the underlying records as public. If authorized access is later provided with explicit reuse terms, assess only the DMI component and keep it separate from the approved USDA/CPER ADG observational case.

sources.title: Deployable DMI prediction using GPBoost, MLOps, and flask without the need for exact birth dates
sources.publicationLicense: Open access article; no separate data license or dataset deposit identified.
sources.reportedPopulation: Beef cattle DMI prediction using animal intake, body weight, age, water behavior, and climate features; the paper reports animal-ID grouped 60:20:20 train/validation/test partitions.
sources.dataAvailabilityStatement: The original contributions presented in the study are included in the article. Further inquiries can be directed to the corresponding author.
sources.publicDataAssessment: No downloadable individual-level dataset, data-specific license, public repository, code repository, or supplementary data package was found on the publisher article page. The article also states that its partitions came from the same broader experimental framework, rather than independent external management, climatic, and geographic settings.
sources.decision: Retain as a peer-reviewed workflow and methods reference only. Article-level metrics and plotted summaries are not individual observations and cannot reproduce the model evaluation. Do not use as an external validation or to calibrate Agroville.

sources.title: Data from Modelling the effect of grazing management of tannin-containing legumes feeding sites on environmental impact by cows grazing grass-dominated rangelands swards
sources.publicationLicense: CC BY 4.0 for the deposited files.
sources.reportedPopulation: A pregnant beef-cow scenario in a grazing-system model, with 25 management/feed scenarios and associated environmental outputs.
sources.dataAvailabilityStatement: The repository deposit is downloadable, but the intake outputs are generated by scenario modelling rather than measured individual-animal observations.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The public files contain synthetic model outputs and scenario-level results, not observed cow-period total-DMI labels with animal and trial identities. The open license does not change their simulated provenance.
sources.decision: Exclude from supervised DMI training and field validation: the deposited DMI values are simulation outputs for scenarios, not observed individual outcomes. Retain only as reusable model-scenario context; do not treat simulated records as measured animal data.

sources.title: Labeled sensor dataset of beef cattle behavior grazing desert rangelands
sources.publicationLicense: CC BY 4.0 for the dataset files.
sources.reportedPopulation: Twenty-four mature beef cows aged 4–9 years monitored on desert rangelands, with per-animal sensor and minute-level grazing-behavior labels.
sources.dataAvailabilityStatement: The data files are publicly downloadable from Figshare under CC BY 4.0.
sources.publicDataAssessment: The deposit provides animal-level behavior/sensor observations but no individual DMI outcome or total-DMI measurement protocol.
sources.decision: Exclude from supervised DMI training and DMI validation: the mature pasture-cow population is relevant, but behavior labels are not DMI outcomes. Retain as a reusable behavior dataset candidate for separate behavior research only.

conclusion: Across the reviewed public candidates, no downloadable, individually reusable adult beef-cattle pasture DMI file with documented data-specific reuse terms and suitable outcome inputs was available for this DMI-focused triage. A separate Dryad grazing-yearling dataset does contain ADG and BW under CC0 but no DMI, so it does not change this conclusion; it is documented in dryad-grazing-yearlings-audit.json and the source table.
limits: A source-level search is not proof that no other dataset exists.
A publication license is not assumed to license its underlying data.
This review does not request access from authors or repositories.
